prompt: The man in the white ruffled collar looks as if he is about to tell you a secret. Write what he says.
Write a letter to the young man in the red cap, small enough to fit inside a locket, telling him what has changed since his day.
The woman in the plaid dress and lace cap folds her hands calmly. Write about a woman in your family who kept her thoughts to herself.
Write a short poem about the young woman with the white headband and the hint of a smile.
The tall woman bends down to the little girl holding the staff. Write what they are saying to each other.
You are the worker standing on the plank beside the carved stone faces. Describe your morning and what you can see from up there.
Describe the crowded harbor with your senses: the creak of the hulls, the smell of tar and water, the rust-colored sails.
The bearded man in the gold chain is glancing sideways at someone. Write the scene: who just walked in, and what does he say?
The old man is filling his long pipe at a small table. Write about someone you knew who had a quiet daily ritual.
Make a list of ten things you would see, hear and smell sitting under the cherry blossoms with Mount Fuji far away.
The man in the feathered hat has a lake and mountains behind him. Write about a view you would want behind your own portrait.
Write a short valentine, in your best handwriting, to someone who would not expect one. Mention the pink rose.
The horse is nosing the ground while two travelers rest at the inn. Where have they come from, and where are they going next?
Write about a piece of lace, a handkerchief or an old tablecloth you remember, and the person who made or kept it.
A huge cloud is building over the hills above the white villa. Write what happens there in the next hour.
Write about an old ruin or building you have visited and what it made you think about time.
Walk along the path toward the stone bridge at sunset. Describe what you hear, smell and feel under your feet.
The young woman with the white ribbon in her hair is sitting for her portrait but thinking about something else. What is it?
Write a short poem about the red circle and the white zigzags, as if the picture were a piece of music.
You are the person poling the small boat under the harvest moon. Tell about your evening on the river.
Two small figures sit on the fallen log above the waterfall. Write what they say to each other over the noise.
Write about a hill or high place where you first saw a whole town or city spread out below you.
The woman is chewing the end of her brush while she thinks. Write the letter she is trying to compose.
You are one of the tall columns. Tell what you have watched from this spot over all the years.
Make a list of ten sounds you would hear in the square on an ordinary morning, with the bell tower and the cart.
The little rowboat is heading out through choppy water toward the tall ships. Who is aboard, and what is the errand?
The two girls in the green hats look up at the tall woman behind them. Write what she just said to them.
The man looks sternly out of the frame. Write about a grandfather or neighbor who seemed strict but turned out to be kind.
Describe the round pink hills and the tiny houses at their feet, as if you had just arrived there on foot.
Write a four line poem to go inside the card, around the little wreath of pink flowers.
You are the swan at the edge of the pond. Describe what you see through the old stone arch.
The woman rests her head on her hand over an enormous book. Write about a book that once kept you reading until you forgot the time.
Behind the louvered shutters the old house is being repaired. Write about who will live there when the work is finished.
